sources.title: Keyulu Xu, Weihua Hu, Jure Leskovec, and Stefanie Jegelka, How Powerful are Graph Neural Networks?, published ICLR 2019 version
sources.locator: Full 17-page published PDF retrieved. Inspected §§2–5 for graph/neighborhood, message-passing, WL, GIN, and mean/max conventions; Lemma 2 and complete Appendix A proof; Theorem 3 and complete Appendix B proof; Lemma 5 and Appendix D; Corollary 6 and Appendix E; and the mean/max results and proofs in Appendices G–H. Appendix I dataset material is excluded.

contents.name: §2 graph, node-feature, aggregation-based GNN, graph-readout, and 1-WL conventions
contents.reason: The local graph definition fixes finite simple undirected graphs, vertex labels, and neighborhoods; its displayed interface supplies the terms used in the local GNN and WL definitions.

contents.name: §2 multiset neighborhood and graph-color histogram conventions
contents.reason: The paper's multiset neighbor and readout operations motivate the generic finite-support multiplicity definition; the local definition supplies the exact equality and size conventions.

contents.name: §2 graph-level readout and Eqs. (2.1), (2.4) message-passing model
contents.reason: The item states the shared aggregation/update and permutation-invariant graph-readout interface with domains and hypotheses explicit.

contents.name: §2 1-WL color refinement and comparison of graph color multisets
contents.reason: The item uses formal ordered-pair colors to make the source's collision-free hash convention explicit.

contents.name: Lemma 2 and complete Appendix A proof: every aggregation-based GNN is bounded by 1-WL
contents.reason: The theorem is reproved locally by induction on color rounds and equality of final state multisets.

contents.name: Theorem 3 and complete Appendix B proof: injective aggregation/update and graph readout match 1-WL
contents.reason: The theorem is reproved locally under explicit injectivity and shared-map hypotheses.

contents.name: §4.1 Eq. (4.1), Lemma 5, Corollary 6, and complete Appendices D–E: GIN update, bounded countable sum encoding, and irrational self-weight
contents.reason: The local proof supplies an explicit integer base code and a full irrational-coefficient argument; the finite-MLP realization limitation is retained.

contents.name: §4.1 GIN sum update and self-weight formula
contents.reason: The definition states the sum update formula and explicitly imposes no injectivity claim on a practical MLP.

contents.name: §5.2 and Appendices G–H: mean and max pooling can collapse multiplicities
contents.reason: The local one-copy/two-copy vector calculation fully verifies the collapse for mean and coordinatewise max.

contents.name: §5 regular-graph limitations and comparison with 1-WL
contents.reason: The local C6 versus two-triangles witness explicitly proves regularity, nonisomorphism, and equal color histograms at every round.

contents.name: §7 benchmark results and Appendix I dataset descriptions
contents.reason: The assigned design excludes empirical graph-classification performance and dataset claims; none is used as theorem evidence.

contents.name: §2 finite graph, labeled graph, isomorphism, neighborhood, multiset, and 1-WL definitions

contents.name: §3 standard 1-GNN aggregation, update, and graph representation; Theorem 1 upper bound
contents.reason: This provides an independent theorem statement and model-convention cross-check; the local proof remains complete.

contents.name: §3 Theorem 2, parameter initialization matching 1-WL, and graph-level readout conventions

contents.name: §3 shared 1-WL/1-GNN limitations and regular-graph color behavior
